hero.title: Abu Dhabi ITC × Navier — a premium, zero-emission layer for an island capital
hero.subtitle: Abu Dhabi is a city of islands. Navier adds a fast, quiet, electric water layer above today's marine fleet — new high-value corridors and a credible path to decarbonize.
hero.what_we_do_together: We work with the Integrated Transport Centre to introduce a software-defined foiling tier on top of Abu Dhabi's existing marine network. Pioneer II runs all-electric across the island core; Quanta-LR opens the long Gulf corridors that today require a road detour. It is additive — premium service and decarbonization — never a displacement of existing operators.

partner_context.their_ambition: As Abu Dhabi's Integrated Transport Centre, you run mobility for a capital that is, literally, a city of islands — Yas, Saadiyat, Al Maryah, Lulu, Reem, Sir Bani Yas and the Corniche — under the Abu Dhabi 2040 urban plan.
partner_context.their_pressure: Connecting your island geography with road and bridge alone is congestion-prone and carbon-heavy; UAE Net Zero 2050 pushes you toward fleet renewal, and your marquee destinations — Saadiyat's museums, Yas events — need premium, reliable access.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier adds a fast, quiet, electric water layer above your existing marine fleet — premium island corridors today's boats can't serve, additive to your current operators.

partner_json_extract.why_now: Abu Dhabi 2040 and UAE Net Zero 2050 give top-cover for marine fleet renewal, and the emirate's geography — Yas, Saadiyat, Al Maryah, Lulu, Sir Bani Yas and the Corniche — is made for water mobility. Foiling makes those hops fast, smooth and silent, with no charging infrastructure required beyond a berth pedestal, and a hybrid long-range option for the Gulf corridor.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
wow_corridors: Abu Dhabi -> Sir Bani Yas / Western Region islands

partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: The marine mode of ITC's integrated network — foiling island hops feeding bus and future rail interchanges, with event-day surge capacity to Yas venues.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined, autonomy-ready, a Turkey factory for regional supply, and a ~100-vessel network proving the model in the Maldives — ready to extend to your islands.

proof_points.evidence: Uber + WeRide robotaxis are deploying in Abu Dhabi — the emirate embraces partner-operated autonomous fleets.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
A Navier vessel is in the UAE now.
proof_points.evidence: A demo vessel is in Dubai — ITC and Abu Dhabi stakeholders can experience the foiling tier on Gulf water before committing.

proof_points.claim: Abu Dhabi is building island destinations faster than road links.
proof_points.evidence: Saadiyat, Yas, Hudayriyat, Lulu and the Western Region islands are all scaling — each one a natural water-corridor node.

objections.response: No — it is a premium tier on island corridors the current fleet doesn't serve, additive to existing services.
Island-core hops are a few nautical miles (Pioneer II); Sir Bani Yas and the Abu Dhabi↔Dubai corridor run on Quanta-LR hybrid range with no charging infrastructure.
Climate-controlled cabins and dramatically lower energy per mile; scheduling flexes around peak summer like every Gulf mode.

objections.concern: Will foiling disturb the mangroves and protected coast?
objections.response: Software-governed no-foil and low-wake zones protect the mangrove channels and shallows; the vessel foils only on cleared open corridors and runs hull-down, low-wake elsewhere — quieter and gentler than today's planing craft.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, the Maldives-proven playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring network integration, berth and event-venue access, and the Abu Dhabi 2040 mandate.
the_ask.next_step: An island-core pilot connecting the Corniche, Saadiyat and Yas.

close.title: A water layer worthy of an island capital.
close.body: From an island-core pilot to a full network to the Gulf corridors, Navier gives Abu Dhabi a premium, zero-emission marine tier — additive to the existing fleet, and a credible path to the emirate's 2040 and Net Zero goals.
